title: Weddings, festivals & occasions
goal: Invite and be invited, know what to say and do at a Kannada wedding, give wishes and blessings, and talk about Ugadi, Sankranti, Ganesha, Dasara, Deepavali and birthdays.
intro:
Karnataka's year is full of occasions: Ugadi in spring, Ganesha and Gowri in the monsoon, Mysuru Dasara in autumn, Deepavali, Sankranti in January, and an endless wedding season in between. Being invited is easy; knowing what to say when you get there is what this unit is for.

The grammar is the language of **wishes and blessings**: the **-ಲಿ** 'may it…' ending (ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದಾಗಲಿ 'may all go well'), the formula ಹಬ್ಬದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು, and how elders bless you. The second point is how to say **'be sure to…'**: ತಪ್ಪದೆ ಬನ್ನಿ 'come without fail', ಬರಲೇಬೇಕು 'you simply must come', ಊಟ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಂಡೇ ಹೋಗಿ 'make sure you eat before you leave'.

vocab.note: Also ಕಲ್ಯಾಣ ಮಂಟಪ. In speech the h is barely heard: 'chatra'.

ಮೈಸೂರು ಮಲ್ಲಿಗೆ, worn in the hair at every function.
ಆಶೀರ್ವಾದ ಮಾಡು 'to bless'.
ನವ ದಂಪತಿಗಳು 'the newly-weds'.

grammar.title: Wishes and blessings: -ಲಿ 'may it…' and ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು
grammar.body:
**The optative -ಲಿ.** Take the infinitive (ಮಾಡ, ಆಗ, ಸಿಗ, ಇರ, ಕೊಡ, ಬರ) and add **-ಲಿ**. It means 'may it…' or 'let it…', and it is the same for every person:
ಆಗು → **ಆಗಲಿ** 'may it happen'
ಸಿಗು → **ಸಿಗಲಿ** 'may (it) be found / may you get'
ಮಾಡು → **ಮಾಡಲಿ** 'may (he) do'
ಇರು → **ಇರಲಿ** 'may (it) be'
ಕೊಡು → **ಕೊಡಲಿ** 'may (he) give'
You met it in unit 18 (ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದಾಗಲಿ) and unit 30 (ಆತ್ಮಕ್ಕೆ ಶಾಂತಿ ಸಿಗಲಿ). The wishes people use all the time:
ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದಾಗಲಿ / ಒಳ್ಳೇದಾಗಲಿ 'all the best' (lit. 'may good happen')
ಶುಭವಾಗಲಿ 'may all go well'
ದೇವರು ಒಳ್ಳೇದು ಮಾಡಲಿ 'God bless you'
ನಿಮ್ಮ ಆಸೆಗಳೆಲ್ಲಾ ಈಡೇರಲಿ 'may all your wishes come true'
ಸುಖವಾಗಿರಲಿ 'may (you / it) be happy'
With a noun or adjective, add **-ಆಗಲಿ** (after -ಅ: -ವಾಗಲಿ): ಶುಭ → ಶುಭವಾಗಲಿ, ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು → ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದಾಗಲಿ.

**'May it not…'**: infinitive + **-ಅದಿರಲಿ**: ಯಾವ ತೊಂದರೆನೂ ಆಗದಿರಲಿ 'may no trouble come'. In speech you'll also hear ಆಗ್ದೇ ಇರ್ಲಿ.

**Blessings from elders** are often polite commands rather than -ಲಿ: ನೂರು ಕಾಲ ಸುಖವಾಗಿ ಬಾಳಿ 'live happily for a hundred years', ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿರಿ / ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿರು 'be well', ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಓದು 'study well'. When you touch an elder's feet you say ಆಶೀರ್ವಾದ ಮಾಡಿ, and they answer with one of these.

**The wishes formula**: occasion + 'of' (-ದ after -ಅ/-ಇ, -ಯ after -ಎ) + **ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು** 'good wishes':
ಯುಗಾದಿ ಹಬ್ಬದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು 'Happy Ugadi'
ಹುಟ್ಟುಹಬ್ಬದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು 'Happy birthday'
ಮದುವೆಯ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು 'congratulations on your wedding'
The reply is **ನಿಮಗೂ** 'to you too' (ನಿಮಗೆ + ಊ 'also'), or ನಿಮಗೂ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು. Among friends English is completely normal: ಹ್ಯಾಪಿ ದೀಪಾವಳಿ, ಹ್ಯಾಪಿ ಬರ್ತ್‌ಡೇ.

**Wishing in your own words**: … ಅಂತ ಹಾರೈಸ್ತೀನಿ 'I wish that …': ನಿನಗೆ ಒಳ್ಳೇದಾಗಲಿ ಅಂತ ಹಾರೈಸ್ತೀನಿ.

examples.en: May all your wishes come true.
May the new year bring you happiness.
Hope you get good marks in the exam.
Be well, child, may God protect you.

grammar.title: 'Be sure to…': ತಪ್ಪದೆ, ಮರೀದೆ, -ಲೇಬೇಕು and the emphatic -ಏ
grammar.body:
English says 'be sure to come', 'don't forget to', 'you must'. Kannada has several ways, from invitation-card formal to friendly insisting.

**1. 'Without …ing': stem + -ಅದೆ.** This negative participle (you saw ಹೇಳದೆ 'without telling' in unit 31) gives the two most common 'be sure to' words:
ತಪ್ಪು 'to miss, fail' → **ತಪ್ಪದೆ** 'without fail'
ಮರೆ 'to forget' → **ಮರೆಯದೆ**, spoken **ಮರೀದೆ** 'without forgetting'
ತಪ್ಪದೆ ಬನ್ನಿ 'be sure to come', ಮರೀದೆ ಫೋನ್ ಮಾಡು 'don't forget to call'. Similar adverbs: **ಕಡ್ಡಾಯವಾಗಿ** 'without fail, absolutely', **ಖಂಡಿತ** 'definitely'.

**2. 'Simply must': infinitive + -ಲೇ + ಬೇಕು.** The emphatic -ಏ goes on the infinitive: ಬರಬೇಕು 'must come' → **ಬರಲೇಬೇಕು** 'you simply must come', ನೋಡಲೇಬೇಕು 'a must-see', ತಿನ್ನಲೇಬೇಕು 'you have to try it'.

**3. 'Make sure you … (before something else)': -ಕೊಂಡು / -ಇ + ಏ.** Put -ಏ on the first verb of a 'do X and then Y' pair: ಊಟ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಂಡು ಹೋಗಿ 'eat and go' → ಊಟ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಂಡೇ ಹೋಗಿ 'don't leave without eating'; ಕಾಫಿ ಕುಡಿದೇ ಹೋಗಿ 'have a coffee before you go'. Hosts say this to every guest.

**4. Promising you definitely will: past form + ಏ + the same verb.** ಬಂದೇ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll definitely come', ಮಾಡೇ ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll do it for sure', ಹೋಗೇ ಹೋಗ್ತೀನಿ 'I'm going, no matter what'. This doubling is very common in friendly speech.

In short: invitation cards say ತಪ್ಪದೆ ಬನ್ನಿ; your friend says ನೀನು ಬರಲೇಬೇಕು ಮಗಾ!; and you reply ಬಂದೇ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ!

examples.en: You have to see the Mysuru Dasara at least once.
Have a coffee before you go.

examples.native: ಈ ಸಲ ಹಬ್ಬಕ್ಕೆ ಊರಿಗೆ ಹೋಗೇ ಹೋಗ್ತೀನಿ
examples.roman: ī sala habbakke ūrige hōgē hōgtīni
examples.en: This time I'm definitely going home for the festival.
Be sure to come to the housewarming.

dialogue.title: At the wedding in Basavanagudi
dialogue.setting: Kavya is at her friend Rahul's wedding at a choultry in Basavanagudi. Arjun arrives late.

lines.speaker: Kavya
lines.native: ಅರ್ಜುನ್! ಬಂದ್ಯಾ? ಮುಹೂರ್ತ ಆಗೇ ಹೋಯ್ತು ಕಣೋ!
lines.roman: arjun! bandyā? muhūrta āgē hōytu kaṇō!
lines.en: Arjun! You made it? The muhurta's already over!

lines.speaker: Arjun

lines.roman: ayyō, ṭrāphik! tāḷi kaṭṭōdu nōḍōke āgalilla.
lines.en: Oh no, the traffic! I missed the tali being tied.

lines.speaker: Kavya
lines.native: ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಬಾ, ಸ್ಟೇಜ್ ಮೇಲೆ ಹೋಗಿ ವಿಶ್ ಮಾಡೋಣ.
lines.roman: paravāgilla, bā, sṭēj mēle hōgi vish māḍōṇa.
lines.en: Never mind, come on, let's go up on stage and wish them.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: ಕಂಗ್ರಾಟ್ಸ್ ರಾಹುಲ್! ಮದುವೆಯ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು, ಸ್ನೇಹಾ ಅವರೇ.
lines.roman: kaṅgrāṭs rāhul! maduveya shubhāshayagaḷu, snēhā avarē.
lines.en: Congrats, Rahul! Congratulations on your wedding, Sneha.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: ಥ್ಯಾಂಕ್ಸ್ ಮಗಾ! ತಡ ಆದ್ರೂ ಬಂದ್ಯಲ್ಲ, ಅದೇ ಖುಷಿ.
lines.roman: thyāṅks magā! taḍa ādrū bandyalla, adē khuṣi.
lines.en: Thanks, man! You came, even if you're late, that's what matters.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: ಇದು ನಮ್ಮ ಕಡೆಯಿಂದ ಒಂದು ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಉಡುಗೊರೆ. ನಿಮ್ಮಿಬ್ಬರಿಗೂ ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದಾಗಲಿ!
lines.roman: idu namma kaḍeyinda ondu chikka uḍugore. nimmibbarigū oḷḷeyadāgali!
lines.en: Here's a little gift from us. All the best to you both!

lines.speaker: Rahul's grandmother
lines.en: Live happily for a hundred years, children.

lines.speaker: Kavya
lines.native: ನೋಡು, ಸ್ನೇಹಾ ರೇಷ್ಮೆ ಸೀರೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಎಷ್ಟು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಕಾಣ್ತಿದ್ದಾಳೆ!
lines.roman: nōḍu, snēhā rēṣme sīreyalli eṣṭu chennāgi kāṇtiddāḷe!
lines.en: Look how lovely Sneha looks in her silk saree!

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: ಹೌದು. ಸರಿ, ಊಟ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? ಹೊಟ್ಟೆ ಹಸೀತಿದೆ.
lines.roman: haudu. sari, ūṭa elli? hoṭṭe hasītide.
lines.en: She does. Right, where's the food? I'm starving.

lines.speaker: Kavya
lines.native: ಕೆಳಗೆ, ಬಾಳೆ ಎಲೆ ಊಟ. ಹೋಳಿಗೆ ತುಪ್ಪ ಕೂಡ ಇದೆ!
lines.roman: keḷage, bāḷe ele ūṭa. hōḷige tuppa kūḍa ide!
lines.en: Downstairs, a banana-leaf meal. There's even holige with ghee!

lines.speaker: Rahul's mother
lines.native: ಊಟ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಂಡೇ ಹೋಗಿ, ಆಯ್ತಾ? ಸಂಜೆ ಆರತಕ್ಷತೆಗೂ ಬನ್ನಿ.
lines.roman: ūṭa māḍkoṇḍē hōgi, āytā? sañje āratakṣategū banni.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.en: Of course, Aunty, we'll definitely be there!

culture:
**Weddings.** Invitations are given in person whenever possible: the family visits with the card and fruit or betel leaves, and says ಕುಟುಂಬ ಸಮೇತ ಬನ್ನಿ. A Hindu wedding in Karnataka usually happens in the morning at a ಛತ್ರ; guests drift in and out, watch the tali being tied at the ಮುಹೂರ್ತ, throw ಅಕ್ಷತೆ (yellow rice) as a blessing, go up on stage to wish the couple and give a gift or cash (in odd amounts: ₹501, ₹1001), and then eat a banana-leaf meal. Leaving without eating is the one real faux pas, hence ಊಟ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಂಡೇ ಹೋಗಿ. Guests are often given ತಾಂಬೂಲ (betel leaves, a coconut, sometimes a small gift) as they leave. Women wear silk sarees and ಮಲ್ಲಿಗೆ in their hair; men wear a kurta or a white ಪಂಚೆ (dhoti).

**Blessings.** At weddings, birthdays and festivals, younger people touch elders' feet (ಕಾಲಿಗೆ ಬೀಳು) and the elder blesses them with ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿರು, ನೂರು ಕಾಲ ಬಾಳು or ದೇವರು ಒಳ್ಳೇದು ಮಾಡಲಿ.

**Festivals.** Ugadi starts the Kannada year with ಬೇವು-ಬೆಲ್ಲ and ಹೋಳಿಗೆ. At Sankranti girls go from house to house exchanging ಎಳ್ಳು-ಬೆಲ್ಲ, saying ಎಳ್ಳು ಬೆಲ್ಲ ತಿಂದು ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಮಾತಾಡಿ. Gowri-Ganesha fills Bengaluru's streets with pandals. Mysuru Dasara, the ನಾಡಹಬ್ಬ, ends with the Jamboo Savari elephant procession. On 1 November, Kannada Rajyotsava, the red-and-yellow Kannada flag is everywhere. Bengaluru and Mangaluru also celebrate Christmas, Eid and the Bengaluru Karaga, and it's normal to greet friends at theirs: ಮೆರಿ ಕ್ರಿಸ್ಮಸ್, ಈದ್ ಮುಬಾರಕ್.

tip.title: Be sure to: ತಪ್ಪದೆ, ಮರೀದೆ, -ಲೇಬೇಕು
tip.body:
- **ತಪ್ಪದೆ** / **ಕಡ್ಡಾಯವಾಗಿ** 'without fail' + verb: ತಪ್ಪದೆ ಬನ್ನಿ.
- **ಮರೀದೆ** (ಮರೆಯದೆ) 'without forgetting': ಮರೀದೆ ಕಳಿಸು.
- 'Simply must' = infinitive + **-ಲೇಬೇಕು**: ನೀವು ಬರ**ಲೇಬೇಕು**.
- 'I'll definitely…' = past + ಏ + verb: **ಬಂದೇ** ಬರ್ತೀನಿ.

sentences.native: ಮುಂದಿನ ತಿಂಗಳು ನನ್ನ ಅಕ್ಕನ ಮದುವೆ, ನೀವು ಬರಲೇಬೇಕು.
sentences.roman: mundina tiṅgaḷu nanna akkana maduve, nīvu baralēbēku.
sentences.en: My sister's wedding is next month, you simply must come.

The muhurta is at half past ten in the morning, be sure to come.

sentences.native: ನಿಶ್ಚಿತಾರ್ಥಕ್ಕೆ ಕಡ್ಡಾಯವಾಗಿ ಬರಬೇಕು ಅಂತ ಅಮ್ಮ ಹೇಳಿದ್ದಾರೆ.

sentences.en: Mum says you absolutely have to come to the engagement.

sentences.en: They've invited us to come with the whole family, without fail.

sentences.en: You look lovely in a silk saree!

tip.title: May it…: -ಲಿ
tip.body:
- Infinitive + **-ಲಿ** = 'may it…': ಆಗು → **ಆಗಲಿ**, ಸಿಗು → **ಸಿಗಲಿ**, ಕೊಡು → **ಕೊಡಲಿ**, ಇರು → **ಇರಲಿ**.
- With a noun: ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು → **ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದಾಗಲಿ**, ಶುಭ → **ಶುಭವಾಗಲಿ**.
- 'May it not': **-ಅದಿರಲಿ**: ತೊಂದರೆ ಆಗದಿರಲಿ.
- Elders also bless with commands: ಸುಖವಾಗಿ **ಬಾಳಿ**.

sentences.en: All the best to you both.
May God give you good health.
Grandma, please bless us.

sentences.native: ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಓದು, ನಿನಗೆ ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಸಿಗಲಿ.
sentences.roman: chennāgi ōdu, ninage oḷḷe kelasa sigali.
sentences.en: Study hard, and may you get a good job.
May God's blessings be with the newly-weds.
May your family always be happy.
May you have no trouble on the journey.
Today is a very auspicious day.
They're looking for an auspicious date for the wedding.

tip.title: Festival wishes: … ಹಬ್ಬದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು
tip.body:
- Occasion + **'of'** + **ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು**: ಯುಗಾದಿ **ಹಬ್ಬದ** ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು, ಮದುವೆ**ಯ** ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು.
- 'Of' is **-ದ** after a, i (ಹಬ್ಬದ, ಹುಟ್ಟುಹಬ್ಬದ) and **-ಯ** after e (ಮದುವೆಯ).
- Reply: **ನಿಮಗೂ** 'to you too'.
- Friends just say ಹ್ಯಾಪಿ ಯುಗಾದಿ!

sentences.en: Happy Sankranti!
Thank you, same to you.
